To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have crystallized a hyperthermophillic DNA polymerase, Pyrococcus furiosisus DNA polymerase (PyrDNApol), from a 3.5 A resolution crystal structure, which will provide a basis for understanding the mechanism by which this enzyme can function at 95 degrees C.
we have crystallized a hyperthermophillic DNA polymerase and that the crystals diffract to 2.5 A resolution.

(1) we have cloned and overexpressed the Pyrococcus furiosis DNA polymerase gene in Eschericha coli; (2) we have purified the protein and crystallized it to 2 A resolution; (3) we have determined the structure of Pyrococcus DNA polymerase to 2 A and have compared it to other DNA polymerases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for producing a highly purified and active DNA polymerase from Pyrococcus furiosisus, a hyperthermophillic archaeon.
the study of the molecular basis of DNA replication and DNA repair.
the purification, crystallization and the preliminary X-ray crystal analysis of Pyrococus furiosus DNA Polymerase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the crystals of Pyrococcus DNA polymerase belong to space group P2(1)2(1) with cell constants a = 92 A, b = 124 A, c = 193 A and with one molecule per asymmetric unit, which gives a solvent content of 53%.

the crystal structure of Pyrococcus DNA polymerase has been solved to a resolution of 2.8 A, and that the structure of the enzyme complexed with a primer/template DNA has been determined to 2.7 A resolution.
the DNA polymerase of Pyrococcus is an unusual and interesting enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first time that a hyperthermophillic archaeal DNA polymerase has been crystallized and that the crystals have diffracted to beyond 4 A.

we have cloned the DNA polymerase gene of Pyrococcus, expressed the protein in E. coli, purified it to apparent homogeneity, crystallized it to high resolution and determined its three-dimensional structure.
we have cloned, overexpressed, purified and crystallized a hyperthermophillic DNA polymerase from Pyrococcus furiose.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a high-throughput screening approach to identify the best crystallization conditions for a particular protein can be a very useful strategy for obtaining crystals of sufficient quality for X-ray diffraction studies.
the DNA polymerase of P. furiosus is a highly thermostable enzyme.
the use of a non-ionic surfactant, NP40, in the crystallization solution is essential in order to obtain good-quality crystals of Pyrococcus DNA polymerase.
